cases.name: gnome-port-chrome-and-menus
cases.prompt: We're porting a Windows desktop app (classic title bar, File/Edit/View/Tools/Help menu bar, toolbar, sidebar) to Linux as a GTK4/libadwaita app aimed at GNOME users. Describe the window chrome, where the menu commands should go, and which standard keys we should support.
cases.trap: Reproducing the Windows title bar plus in-window menu bar on GNOME, or using Super-key shortcuts, instead of a header bar with a primary menu.
expectations: Uses a header bar (client-side decorations) as the window chrome instead of a separate title bar plus menu bar
Places secondary/app-level commands (Preferences, Keyboard Shortcuts, About) in a primary menu button in the header bar
Names F10 as opening the primary menu
Names Ctrl+? as opening a keyboard shortcuts window
Mentions F9 for toggling the sidebar or F1 for help
States that the Super key must not be used for app shortcuts
Requires every action to be reachable by keyboard
negative_expectations: Recommends keeping a traditional File/Edit/View in-window menu bar as the primary GNOME pattern
Assigns any application shortcut using the Super key

cases.name: tauri-state-persistence-spec
cases.prompt: Tauri 2 photo-culling app for macOS, Windows and Linux. Users open a folder of RAW files, flag/reject images, and zoom per image. Write the state-persistence part of the design spec: what is remembered between launches, where, and what first launch and an unexpected crash look like.
cases.trap: Assuming the OS or framework restores window and session state automatically, mixing per-image zoom with global preferences, and skipping first-launch and crash-recovery design.
expectations: Separates state into categories: ephemeral (not restored), session (restored on relaunch), user preferences, and per-document/per-image state
Lists window size/position, open folder, panel visibility/sizes and current selection or scroll as restored session state
Treats per-image zoom as document-level state, not a global preference
States that Tauri does not restore session state automatically and names an explicit mechanism such as tauri-plugin-window-state and/or tauri-plugin-store
Specifies the first-launch experience (empty state or onboarding, defaults taken from system settings such as dark mode)
Specifies crash detection on next launch and an offer to restore or discard unsaved flags
negative_expectations: Claims the OS will automatically restore the app's windows and open folder for a Tauri app
